labels.ip_host: Uses a raw IP address instead of a name
labels.n_subdomains: Many subdomains hiding the real owner
labels.at_symbol: Contains '@', which can redirect the link
labels.digits_host: Numbers mixed into the domain name
labels.digit_ratio: Lots of numbers in the link
labels.longest_host_token: Unusually long word in the domain
labels.brand_in_path: Brand name buried in the path, not the domain
labels.brand_in_sub: Brand or school name in a subdomain
labels.php_or_html: Points straight at a script or file
labels.brand_dist: Domain is spelled almost like a trusted name
labels.vowel_ratio: Domain name doesn't read like a word
labels.digits_sld: Numbers mixed into the domain name
labels.n_params: Lots of tracking or query parameters
labels.free_host: Hosted on a free website service anyone can use

text_flags.name: urgency
text_flags.label: Urgent or pressure language
text_flags.why: Scammers rush you so you act before you think.

text_flags.name: threat
text_flags.label: Threat of losing access
text_flags.why: Real offices rarely threaten to shut your account by email.

text_flags.name: credential_request
text_flags.label: Asks for your password or login
text_flags.why: No campus office will ask you to confirm a password through a link or reply.

text_flags.name: sensitive_info
text_flags.label: Requests personal or banking details
text_flags.why: Requests for SSN, bank or card numbers by email are a classic scam.
patterns: \bseguro social\b|\bcuenta bancaria\b|\btarjeta de (credito|debito)\b|\bnumero de (cuenta|tarjeta)\b|\bfecha de nacimiento\b
\bnumero de securite sociale\b|\bcompte bancaire\b|\bcarte (bancaire|de credit)\b|\bdate de naissance\b

text_flags.name: click_cta
text_flags.label: Pushes you to click a link or open a file
text_flags.why: The whole message exists to get you to one link or attachment.

text_flags.name: impersonation
text_flags.label: Claims to be an official office or service
text_flags.why: Phishers borrow the name of IT, Financial Aid, banks and big brands.

text_flags.name: money_lure
text_flags.label: Too-good-to-be-true money or prize
text_flags.why: Unexpected money, prizes or easy pay are bait.

text_flags.name: job_scam
text_flags.label: Easy remote job offer
text_flags.why: Unsolicited, flexible, high-pay jobs are a top student scam.

text_flags.name: asks_for_secrets
text_flags.label: Asks you to send passwords, codes or personal info
text_flags.why: Legit people and offices never need you to send a password, code, card or ID number in a message.
patterns: \b(send|reply with|provide|give|enter|submit|share|text|tell me|confirm|forward|type in|input)\b[^.!?\n]{0,40}\b(password|login|log-in|credentials|ssn|social security|bank|card number|cvv|date of birth|student id|id number|username|user name|pin|passcode|verification code|6[- ]digit code|the code|fsa id|routing)\b
\b(password|login|ssn|bank login|card details|verification code|the code)\b[^.!?\n]{0,25}\b(to me|so (i|we) can|to verify|to confirm|to receive)\b

text_flags.name: upfront_payment
text_flags.label: Asks you to pay first or move money
text_flags.why: Paying a fee, buying gift cards or forwarding money to 'unlock' something is how advance-fee scams work.

text_flags.name: generic_greeting
text_flags.label: Generic greeting
text_flags.why: Messages from real offices usually use your name.

text_flags.name: secrecy
text_flags.label: Asks you to keep it secret or reply privately
text_flags.why: Legit offices do not ask for secrecy or replies to personal accounts.

text_flags.name: gift_card_request
text_flags.label: Asks you to buy gift cards or send card codes
text_flags.why: No professor, boss or office will ask you to buy gift cards and send the codes. Once the codes are sent, the money is gone.
patterns: \b(buy|purchase|buying|purchasing)\b[^.!?\n]{0,50}\b(gift ?cards?|itunes( cards?)?|google play( cards?)?|steam( wallet)?( cards?)?|apple cards?|ebay cards?|amazon cards?|visa gift|vanilla (gift )?cards?)\b

\b(can you|could you|i need you to|need you to|please|i want you to|help me|would you)\b[^.!?\n]{0,30}\b(get|pick up|grab|order|go get)\b[^.!?\n]{0,50}\b(gift ?cards?|itunes( cards?)?|google play( cards?)?|steam( wallet)?( cards?)?|apple cards?|ebay cards?|amazon cards?|visa gift|vanilla (gift )?cards?)\b
\b(i need|i'll need|need you to get|we need)\b[^.!?\n]{0,30}\b(gift ?cards?|itunes( cards?)?|google play( cards?)?|steam( wallet)?( cards?)?|apple cards?|amazon cards?)\b

text_flags.name: unavailable_pretext
text_flags.label: Sender says they can't talk and wants a quick favor
text_flags.why: Impersonators say they are in a meeting or can't call so you won't check with the real person.
patterns: \bje suis en reunion\b|\bje ne peux pas (parler|appeler)\b

url_ip_host: Link uses a raw IP address
Real sites use names, not numbers like 192.168.0.1.
url_lookalike: The domain imitates a trusted name (e.g. aamu-support.com).
url_many_subdomains: Long chains like login.aamu.edu.verify.xyz hide the real owner.
url_shortener: bit.ly-style links hide where you will land.
url_suspicious_tld: Endings like .xyz, .ru, .top are common in scams.
url_at_or_redirect: Characters that make a link go somewhere other than it looks.
url_sensitive_words: Words like 'secure-login-verify' in a link are a warning sign.
url_non_campus_official: It claims to be the school but its links go elsewhere.
sender_freemail_official: Official request from a personal email
Campus offices write from @aamu.edu, not Gmail or Yahoo.
shouting: SHOUTING and !!! are used to create panic.
n_urls: Bait messages are built around links.
sender_lookalike: Sender address imitates a trusted domain
The From address looks official but isn't (e.g. @aamu-support.com).
sender_display_mismatch: Sender name doesn't match their address
It says it's from the school or a brand, but the address belongs to someone else.
sender_freemail: Official-sounding sender using a personal mailbox
Offices and companies don't send official notices from Gmail/Yahoo.
sender_trusted_risky_request: Official address, but a risky request
Real offices never ask for passwords, codes or payments by message. A hacked account can send from a real address.
category_notice_personal_mailbox: Account or delivery notice from a personal mailbox
Companies send delivery and account notices from their own domain, not from Gmail, Yahoo or Outlook addresses.
category_fake_social: Looks like a social notification, but isn't from that site
It reads like a notification from a social site, but the sender's address belongs to someone else.

actions.sender_lookalike: Delete it. The sender is pretending to be a trusted address. If unsure, contact the office through aamu.edu.
actions.credential_request: Don't enter your password anywhere this message sends you. Type the official address yourself instead.
actions.sensitive_info: Never send SSN, bank, card or ID details by email or text. Call the office using a number from the official website.
actions.url_lookalike: Don't click. The link only looks like a trusted address.
actions.job_scam: Real campus jobs are posted through Career Services or Handshake. Don't reply to personal email addresses or send money.
actions.gift_card_request: Don't buy anything. Contact the person through a phone number or office you already know, not by replying. Gift-card codes can't be recovered once sent.
actions.money_lure: Unexpected money or prizes that need a fee or your details are scams. Don't reply.
actions.impersonation: If it claims to be a campus office, contact that office directly through aamu.edu, not through the message.
actions.sender_freemail: Official offices don't write from Gmail/Yahoo. Contact the office through its official website.
actions.sender_display_mismatch: The sender name and address don't match. Verify through an official channel before doing anything.
actions.sender_trusted_risky_request: Don't send anything. The address is real, but offices never ask for this by message, so the account may be hacked. Call or visit the office using contact details from aamu.edu.

infer.default_action: Don't click links or reply. Report it to the campus IT help desk.
infer.safe_action: No strong warning signs. If anything still feels off, contact the sender through an official channel.
